fields.decision: What Spoke builds next quarter to grow bookings

frames.name: Goal

draft.question: Is this the goal, or is there one above it?
draft.proposal: Grow app downloads, because the brief says the app needs more users.

fields.user_problem: Riders do not know the app exists

frames.answer: Downloads are not the goal. A shop pays us when a repair gets booked. The goal is first bookings that complete.
frames.change: From downloads to completed first bookings: it is what the shops pay for and what a rider came to do.

final.business_goal: More riders complete a first repair booking
final.user_problem: A rider with a broken bike cannot tell which shop can fix it this week or what it will cost
final.why_now: Two shop chains asked for a pilot this spring
final.brief_and_givens: Decide what to build next quarter, with the current team. Shops keep their own tools during the pilot.

frames.name: Customer

draft.question: Why this customer and not the other?
draft.proposal: Weekend riders, because there are more of them.

frames.answer: Commuters. A weekend rider can wait a week. A commuter with a flat loses the workday, so the urgency is theirs.
frames.change: From weekend riders to daily commuters: fewer people, but the repair blocks their day and they come back.

final.chosen_why: We assume commuters are 60% of repair demand and the only group that needs the bike back the same day

frames.name: Where it fails today

draft.question: These three, or is one missing?
draft.proposal: No visible slots, unknown price, and a day without the bike, ranked by how often they stop a booking.

failures.name: No visible slots
failures.cause: Shops keep their week on paper
failures.alternative_today: Calls two or three shops, or rides to the nearest one and waits

failures.name: Unknown price
failures.alternative_today: Asks a friend or accepts the quote at the counter

failures.name: A day without the bike
failures.alternative_today: Takes the bus or borrows a bike

frames.name: Ideas

draft.question: Which one would you add?
draft.proposal: Three ideas of different size, one per failure.

frames.answer: Add pickup at the office. Some commuters cannot even get the bike to the shop.
frames.change: A fourth idea, office pickup, for the commuter who cannot reach the shop.

frames.name: Choose, hypothesis and metrics

draft.question: Is this the idea that moves the goal most, and is this how we would know?
draft.proposal: The calendar, measured by how many riders open it.

fields.why_vs_goal: It removes the first reason a booking does not start

hypothesis.statement: If commuters see this week's slots, more of them book

metrics.secondary: Time from opening the app to a confirmed slot
metrics.guardrails: Shop no-shows and cancellations do not rise

fields.cheap_test: Three shops update a shared sheet every morning
fields.weak_spot: It depends on shops keeping the calendar current

frames.answer: The calendar, yes. But views are not the metric. Count how many started bookings complete.
frames.change: Primary metric from calendar views to the share of started bookings that complete: views can grow while bookings do not.

final.why_vs_goal: It removes the first reason a booking does not start

hypothesis.statement: If commuters see this week's slots, more started bookings complete

metrics.primary: Share of started bookings that complete
metrics.secondary: Time from opening the app to a confirmed slot
metrics.guardrails: Shop no-shows and cancellations do not rise

final.cheap_test: Three shops update a shared sheet every morning
final.weak_spot: It depends on shops keeping the calendar current
